The colorimeter sensitivity doubled overnight
Samples became more coloured that week
The verified stock has lost strength

inference.explanation: Slope doubles with the suspect stock and returns to normal with verified stock, and the bottle is shown to be a relabelled 1000 unit concentrate. Instrument checks pass, so the error is stock strength, not the meter or samples.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the stock mix up?

options.label: Standard stock inventory and relabelling log for the shelf reorganization
Colorimeter service report
Raw water colour trend

nextClue.explanation: The inventory and relabelling log trace which concentrate went into the 500 unit bottle.

clueText.nc-b: The service report is routine, matching the passing instrument checks.
clueText.nc-c: Raw colour was steady, while results changed only with the suspect curve.

evidence.label: The colour development reagent was mixed at the start of the day and left in a clear bottle on the bench.

The spectrophotometer wavelength and blank checks pass at hour four.
Standards and samples use the same reagent in each run, so calibration standards drift with the samples.

The spectrophotometer lamp faded over four hours
Ammonia volatilized from all samples equally in four hours
The analyst pipetting technique worsened during the day

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms reagent degradation?

Pipette calibration record

clueText.nc-b: Lamp hours are within life and fresh reagent passes on the same lamp.

tasks.prompt: A balance used for standard preparation reads 0.1000 g correctly but a 1.0000 g check weight reads 0.9820 g.

Drafts and vibration were controlled during the checks.

options.label: The balance has a span error at higher loads, so standards weighed near 1 g are understated
The 1 g check weight has lost mass
The second balance is miscalibrated at both points
Air drafts caused a one time low reading

inference.explanation: The low point passes while the high point reads low, certified weights read correctly on a second balance, and prepared standards are low by the same proportion. That is a span error, not the weight, the second balance, or a draft.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the span error?

options.label: Balance calibration history showing linearity checks across the working range
Check weight purchase record
Laboratory draft survey

nextClue.explanation: Linearity history shows whether error grows with load on this balance.

clueText.nc-a: History shows error growing from near zero at 0.1 g to minus 2 percent at 1 g over three months, confirming a progressive span error.
clueText.nc-b: The purchase record confirms certification that the second balance verified.
clueText.nc-c: Draft controls were in place for both balances, yet only one failed.

The stock standard is nonlinear in response
The meter response is inherently curved at low chlorine
The dilution water consumes chlorine unevenly

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the pipette error?

options.label: Pipette gravimetric calibration records by volume setting
Stock titration certificate
Meter linearity specification

nextClue.explanation: Calibration records by setting show whether the 1 mL setting was already out of tolerance.

clueText.nc-b: The stock certificate matches the titration verification done today.
clueText.nc-c: The meter specification is linear, matching the volumetric standard results.

Seed culture purchase record

The issued report lists the home laboratory method code and no subcontractor disclosure.
The disclosure procedure in the quality file requires identifying subcontracted results on the report.
Bench logs show no analysis of the sample in the home laboratory.
The numerical result itself matches the subcontractor value and is technically valid.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: The report misattributes a subcontracted result to the home laboratory method, breaching disclosure procedure
The home laboratory analysed the sample but lost its bench log
Subcontractor results never need disclosure when values match
The method code difference is a harmless formatting choice

inference.explanation: Bench logs show no home analysis, the subcontractor report exists, and procedure requires disclosure that the issued report omits. That is misattribution, not a lost log, an exemption, or formatting.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms misattribution?

options.label: Subcontractor report, bench log absence, and disclosure procedure for the sample
Issued report alone
Subcontractor invoice alone

nextClue.explanation: The three records together prove source, absence, and the disclosure duty.

clueText.nc-a: The subcontractor report matches the value, no bench entry exists, and procedure requires disclosure, confirming misattribution.
clueText.nc-b: The issued report alone cannot reveal its own source error.
clueText.nc-c: The invoice shows a business relation but not this sample's path.

tasks.prompt: Trend charts in a quality review show improving chlorine residuals, but the chart plots only weekday results while weekend low results sit in a separate unplotted file.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario drinking water laboratory case under Regulation 169/03 and Regulation 170/03. All results are from the stated batch unless noted, and archived laboratory records are available for review.

evidence.label: Weekend values average 0.25 mg/L lower than weekday values in the raw data.
The chart data range in the spreadsheet covers Monday to Friday rows only.
No procedure authorizes excluding weekend operational samples from trend review.
Both files come from the same validated results database.
Analyser and sampling QC are equivalent on weekends and weekdays.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: The trend review is misleading because weekend results were excluded from the plotted data without authorization
Weekend residuals truly do not belong to the same system
The database weekend file contains invalid results
Weekday only plotting is the required review method

inference.explanation: Weekend data are valid, from the same database and system, materially lower, and no procedure authorizes exclusion, yet the chart range omits them. That is a misleading selective trend, not separate systems, invalid data, or a required method.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms selective plotting?

options.label: Spreadsheet chart data range and the complete database extract for the period
Weekend staffing roster
Chart title page

nextClue.explanation: Chart range against the full extract proves the omission quantitatively.

clueText.nc-a: The range covers weekdays only while the full extract shows lower weekend values for every week, confirming selective plotting.
clueText.nc-b: Staffing does not determine data validity for trending.
clueText.nc-c: The title page claims a full period trend that the range contradicts.

tasks.prompt: An analyst develops eye irritation after preparing a standard, and the safety data review finds the acid used was a concentrated stock decanted into an unlabelled spray bottle.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario drinking water laboratory case under Regulation 169/03 and Regulation 170/03. All results are from the stated batch unless noted, and archived laboratory records are available for review.

evidence.label: The spray bottle has no label, hazard, or concentration marking, confirmed by photo.
The laboratory procedure in the safety file requires original or fully labelled secondary containers only.
Other analysts report using the same bottle believing it was dilute rinse solution.
Ventilation and eyewash checks are current and the eyewash was used promptly.
No spill or breakage occurred; exposure was by spray mist during normal use.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: Decanting concentrated acid into an unlabelled spray bottle created an unrecognized hazard that caused the exposure
The eyewash station failure caused the irritation
The analyst's own dilute standard preparation was the hazard
Ventilation failure concentrated vapours in the room

inference.explanation: The bottle is unlabelled concentrate mistaken for dilute solution, procedure prohibits it, and eyewash and ventilation are verified working with prompt use. That is a labelling and decanting failure, not eyewash, personal preparation, or ventilation causes.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the container hazard?

options.label: Container inspection photos and secondary container labelling procedure audit
Eyewash inspection log
Ventilation test report

nextClue.explanation: Photos plus the labelling audit establish the unlabelled concentrate in service.

clueText.nc-a: Photos show the unlabelled spray bottle and the audit finds two more unlabelled secondary containers, confirming a systemic labelling failure.
clueText.nc-b: Eyewash inspections pass and it was used promptly, clearing it.
clueText.nc-c: Ventilation tests pass, arguing against vapour concentration.

tasks.prompt: A chlorine gas alarm sounds in the standards room, and a leaking compressed gas cylinder is found with its regulator hand tightened only.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario drinking water laboratory case under Regulation 169/03 and Regulation 170/03. All results are from the stated batch unless noted, and archived laboratory records are available for review.

evidence.label: The cylinder is a chlorine calibration gas cylinder used for a bench standard system.
The regulator connection shows no wrench marks and a soap test bubbles at the fitting.
A second cylinder installed with a wrench and leak tested shows no leak.
The alarm and ventilation interlock function correctly and the room was evacuated promptly.
Cylinder storage, chaining, and cap records are otherwise in order.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: The hand tightened regulator connection leaked chlorine gas, triggering the alarm
The alarm is a false positive with no actual leak
The cylinder valve body itself has failed internally
Ventilation failure allowed normal background chlorine to accumulate

inference.explanation: Soap testing bubbles at the hand tightened fitting, a properly installed cylinder does not leak, and safety systems worked. That is a connection leak, not a false alarm, internal valve failure, or ventilation cause.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the connection leak?

options.label: Leak test results and cylinder installation checklist for the standards room
Alarm calibration certificate alone
Ventilation interlock test

nextClue.explanation: Leak testing at the fitting is the direct localization evidence.

clueText.nc-a: Soap tests bubble only at the regulator fitting and stop after wrench tightening and retest, confirming the connection leak.
clueText.nc-b: The alarm certificate supports the alarm, but the leak test localizes the source.
clueText.nc-c: The interlock passed, matching the prompt evacuation.

tasks.prompt: Repeated low level solvent odours are traced to waste bottles stored uncapped beside a hot plate in the organics preparation area.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario drinking water laboratory case under Regulation 169/03 and Regulation 170/03. All results are from the stated batch unless noted, and archived laboratory records are available for review.

evidence.label: Three waste bottles are found with caps off or loosely placed on top.
The hot plate surface beside them is at 80 C during extractions.
The safety file procedure requires waste containers closed except when actively adding waste.
Room ventilation readings are within design and the fume hood face velocity passes.
No spill has occurred; odour strength rises when the hot plate is on.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: Open waste bottles near a heat source evaporate solvent into the room, breaching the closed container rule
The fume hood has failed and is releasing vapours
A waste bottle has cracked and is leaking liquid
Ventilation design is undersized for the room

inference.explanation: Caps are off, heat is adjacent, odour tracks hot plate use, and ventilation and hood checks pass with no liquid leak. That is evaporation from open containers, not hood, crack, or design failures.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the open container cause?

options.label: Waste storage inspection and odour log correlated with hot plate use
Fume hood face velocity report
Waste bottle purchase specification

nextClue.explanation: Inspection findings correlated with odour timing isolate the open bottles.

clueText.nc-a: Inspections find caps off on three bottles and odour peaks match hot plate operating hours, confirming evaporation from open waste.
clueText.nc-b: Hood velocity passes, clearing hood failure.
clueText.nc-c: Bottle specifications do not address caps left off in service.

tasks.prompt: A quality review finds the same control chart warning ignored for five batches, with control values trending toward the limit but no action recorded.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario drinking water laboratory case under Regulation 169/03 and Regulation 170/03. All results are from the stated batch unless noted, and archived laboratory records are available for review.

evidence.label: The control chart shows five consecutive points on one side of the mean, the warning rule stated in the quality file.
Each batch was released without a documented investigation.
The control material, instrument, and calibration are later shown to be in control after a reagent change.
Values never exceeded the action limit, so no batch failed outright.
Other charts in the same review show warnings actioned with notes.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: The laboratory failed to act on a defined control chart warning rule across five batches
No action was needed because the action limit was never crossed
The control material was drifting and the chart is invalid
Trending on one side of the mean carries no rule in the quality system

inference.explanation: The quality file defines the five point warning rule, the chart meets it, releases lack investigations, and peer charts show the rule being actioned. Staying inside the action limit does not cancel a warning rule, and later control recovery does not invalidate the chart.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the missed warning action?

options.label: Control chart with the quality file warning rule and batch release records
Control material certificate
Instrument calibration log

nextClue.explanation: Chart, rule, and release records together prove the missed required action.

clueText.nc-a: Five points sit on one side per the stated rule and all five releases lack investigation notes, confirming the miss.
clueText.nc-b: The certificate does not address chart rule application.
clueText.nc-c: Calibration was later verified, supporting chart validity.

tasks.prompt: An analyst certificate review finds bench work was performed for two weeks by a trainee whose supervised practice log was never signed off for the microbiology method.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario drinking water laboratory case under Regulation 169/03 and Regulation 170/03. All results are from the stated batch unless noted, and archived laboratory records are available for review.

evidence.label: The trainee performed the method independently on night shifts, per the roster.
The training file shows classroom completion but no signed practical sign off for that method.
Regulation 128/04 analyst certification context in the quality file requires demonstrated competency before independent work.
QC samples run by the trainee happened to pass, but no competency assessment is recorded.
Other analysts on the method all hold signed sign offs.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: Independent bench work was assigned before documented competency sign off, a quality system breach regardless of passing QC
Passing QC samples retroactively complete the sign off
Classroom completion alone authorizes independent method work
Night shift work does not count as independent practice

inference.explanation: The roster shows independent work, the file lacks practical sign off, and the quality file requires demonstrated competency first. Passing QC does not substitute for assessment, classroom alone is insufficient per the file, and night work is still independent practice.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the competency gap?

options.label: Training file and shift roster for the trainee on the method
QC results log alone
Classroom attendance record alone

nextClue.explanation: Training file against roster proves work preceded sign off.

clueText.nc-a: The file shows no practical sign off while the roster shows two weeks of independent night shifts, confirming the gap.
clueText.nc-b: QC passes show luck or skill but not documented competency.
clueText.nc-c: Classroom attendance is present, yet practical sign off is the missing requirement.

tasks.prompt: Broken glass injuries recur in one preparation area, and inspection finds a sharps and glass disposal bin overfilled with glass protruding above the rim.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario drinking water laboratory case under Regulation 169/03 and Regulation 170/03. All results are from the stated batch unless noted, and archived laboratory records are available for review.

evidence.label: Three minor cuts in two months are all recorded in that preparation area.
The disposal procedure in the safety file requires replacing bins at the fill line, well below the rim.
The bin in use is filled above the rim with protruding broken pipettes.
Gloves, tongs, and bench training records for the area are current.
Other preparation areas with bins at proper fill levels report no injuries.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: The overfilled glass disposal bin exposes analysts to protruding glass and explains the recurring cuts
Analysts in that area need retraining on glass handling
The pipette glass itself is unusually brittle
Injuries are random and unrelated to area conditions

inference.explanation: Injuries cluster where the bin is overfilled past its procedure limit with protruding glass, training is current, and other areas at proper fill have no injuries. That is a disposal hazard, not training, glass quality, or chance.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the disposal hazard?

options.label: Bin inspection photos and injury log by preparation area
Glassware supplier specification
Training attendance log

nextClue.explanation: Photos plus area injury pattern localize the hazard.

clueText.nc-a: Photos show glass above the rim and all three injuries map to that area and bin, confirming the hazard.
clueText.nc-b: The same glassware is used in injury free areas, clearing brittleness.
clueText.nc-c: Training is current for the injured analysts, clearing the training theory.
